results.title: Acrobat AI Assistant: One Year Later | Deep Analysis
results.content:
A key finding of the Blockchain report was lifted from another report. AI Assistant missed the most obvious answer, a sentence containing “the single biggest stumbling block to its adoption”.
 One of the IDP report findings was sourced from the footnotes of another report.
 Several other attribution problems were encountered.

Double check the math. When asked to calculate the total revenue size of all markets in 2027, AI Assistant miscalculated the revenue for one of the markets, which led to a $3 billion over-estimation.

### Overall Impressions

Acrobat’s new AI Assistant is a welcome upgrade from the old and frustrating Find search feature. But Adobe didn’t go to all this trouble just to give you a better search experience. [...] The warnings go on. Adobe also addresses the link attribution problem I encountered: “Attribution can take the form of clickable citations or other helpful cues indicating where generated information came from. However, because the AI Assistant is powered by generative AI models, and the technology is still evolving and not perfect, not all answers are helpful or accurate. For example, you may receive a clickable citation or cue that takes you to an unrelated section instead of providing helpful information on where the answer came from in the document. Please double-check all AI-generated responses.” [...] Thankfully Adobe has replaced that annoying feature with a new “How can I help you with this document” followed by three icon choices: Understand, Analyze, or Generate. The product team wisely included the meaning of each choice in the hover-over bubbles, so I didn’t have to guess. I tried Understand first to see key highlight questions and I was pleased with the results (Fig. 2).

Fig. 2 Understand

I tested the first question, an easy one since I knew the report contains an obvious list inside. AI Assistant generated an accurate list with links to each source (Fig. 3). However the attribution links were insufficient for explaining how AI Assistant gathered the response, often taking me to an unrelated sentence.

Fig. 3 Suggested question
